newsitem.title: USA: Occidental sees higher oil, gas earnings.
newsitem.headline: Occidental sees higher oil, gas earnings.

text.p: Occidental Petroleum Corp said it expects oil and natural gas earnings before special items to total at least $550 million in 1996, more than double the $249 million earned last year.

The company said that Chairman Ray Irani, speaking to analysts in New York, also said worldwide operating costs declined to an estimated $5.40 per barrel of oil equivalent this year from $5.52 last year and $6.07 in 1993.
Irani projected capital spending at about $1.1 billion in 1997, up from $1 billion in 1996.
About 65 percent of the total spending budget will go to oil and gas, 25 percent to chemicals, and the remainder to its domestic Midcon natural gas transmission division.

Irani also told analysts Occidental has reduced interest expense by more than half since 1990 to an estimated $460 million this year. He said Occidental's long-term debt is expected to be $4.5 billion by year-end and debt-to-capitalization is expected to be 49 percent.

He said another goal of the company is to "achieve significant growth in profitability in all our businesses." In the chemicals sector, he said the comany has established a target floor of $600 million for earnings and is taking steps to mitigate earning volatility.
The chemicals division also plans to increase chlor-alkali manufacturing capacity by 580 tons per day over the next two years.

Also at the analysts' meeting, MidCon President and Chief Executive Officer John Riordan said that division's earnings before special items shuold exceed $270 million in 1996, up from $250 million in 1995.
